sections.h2: What does selling a house in Grove City, Ohio involve?
sections.html:
Grove City sellers choose between a retail listing, a sale they handle themselves, and a direct cash purchase. All three pass through the same state disclosure statute and the same Franklin County deed desk, so the decision turns on how much time you have and what shape the house is in.

The housing here runs from older frame homes near Broadway to subdivisions that went up as Columbus spread south and west. A tidy exterior and a clean code record help in any of those pockets, which is why much of this page covers what the city inspects and what Ohio law makes a seller put in writing.

sections.h2: Where is Grove City and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Grove City lies in southeastern Franklin County, a short drive from downtown Columbus. William F. Breck platted the village east of Broadway in 1852 because the Harrisburg Turnpike already ran toward the capital. The settlers named the place for the groves of trees they left standing when they cleared the land.

The state recognized a village on March 5, 1866, and a city in 1959. The Census Bureau counted 35,575 people in 2010 and 41,252 in 2020, with 45,180 in its 2025 estimate.

A charter written in 1958 and amended in 1982 sets up an elected mayor and council plus an appointed administrator. The city keeps its own police division, which holds national accreditation. Jackson Township staffs four fire stations that cover the city and the township together.

sections.h2: Who lives in Grove City and what do Census figures show about its homes?
sections.html:
Owners live in roughly seven of every ten Grove City homes, and the median owner-occupied value passes $300,000 in the five-year Census estimates. Buyers in that range expect a house that needs little work, so deferred repairs weigh heavily on offers.

Residents 65 and older make up 18.8% of the city, the largest share among the four Ohio cities in that Census release. Long-time owners moving to smaller quarters and heirs settling an estate account for a steady flow of sales.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Grove City homes?
sections.html:
The South-Western City School District serves Grove City, with Grove City High School and Central Crossing High School inside the city. Beulah Park, Jackson and Pleasant View are the middle schools, Hayes, Park Street and Holt Crossing are the intermediate schools, and the district also runs eight elementary schools and the South-Western Career Academy there.

Families can also look at Grove City Christian, Our Lady of Perpetual Help School and Beautiful Savior Lutheran School. Ask the district to confirm the attendance zone for your address before a listing names a school.

sections.h2: What city rules apply to a Grove City property before a sale?
sections.html:
The Building and Zoning Division enforces the Grove City municipal code alongside the International Code Council Property Maintenance Code, and inspectors walk the community checking exteriors. Correcting visible problems early keeps an open citation from surfacing in a buyer's inspection.

  • Grass and weeds stay under six inches, with an exception for cultivated flowers and gardens. Noxious weeds are banned outright.
  • A vehicle that cannot run belongs in a garage or off the lot.
  • The city encourages owners to check siding, roofs, gutters and downspouts for damage every year.
  • The division answers questions at 614-277-3075 and takes complaints through an online form.

Its forms page covers new structures, additions, pools, fences, driveways, sidewalks and mechanical work. If earlier owners did work on the house, ask the division whether the permits were closed. The code compliance page lists the current standards.

sections.h2: What must a Grove City seller put in writing under Ohio law?
sections.html:
Section 5302.30 of the Ohio Revised Code makes a seller of a one to four unit home complete a state form and give each prospective buyer a signed copy. The form asks about the water supply, sewer or septic system, roof, foundation, walls, floors, lead paint, asbestos, radon and any material defect you know of.

  • Answer from your own knowledge. Where a fact is unknown, a good-faith estimate is acceptable.
  • A buyer who first sees the form after signing has three business days from receipt to cancel.
  • A buyer who never gets the form can cancel until the sooner of 30 days after acceptance or closing.
  • You may amend the form in writing after you deliver it.

Court-ordered sales, foreclosure sales and sales by an executor or trustee fall outside the rule. The statute lists every exemption.

sections.h2: How does the deed move through the Franklin County Auditor?
sections.html:
A Grove City deed goes to the Franklin County Auditor's Transfer and Conveyance Department for a stamp and fee before the county recorder files it. The conveyance fee is $3 for each $1,000 of price, made up of $1 set by Ohio and $2 set by the Franklin County commissioners, plus a $0.50 transfer tax and a $3 minimum.

  • The price is rounded up to the next $100 for the calculation.
  • A grantor who holds the homestead exemption at transfer pays only $1 per $1,000.
  • Call the department at 614-525-3253 with questions.

The Auditor's online calculator returns the amount for a given price. Your title company will tell you whether it handles the Auditor visit at closing.

sections.h2: Which sale route suits a Grove City house?
sections.html:
A retail listing makes sense for a house in showing condition when you can wait through an ordinary marketing period. Selling alone suits an owner who already reads contracts and knows what comparable homes in Jackson Township and the city have brought. A cash purchase fits an inherited house, a rental with tenants in place, or a property with deferred work and a firm moving date.

Weigh any written offer against the net you would keep after repairs, closing costs and the monthly cost of holding the house, and read the contract in full before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Grove City house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio does not require repairs before a sale, but you must disclose known defects on the state form. Buyers may lower their price or ask for credits, and a cash buyer will usually take the house as it is. Clear any open code violations with the city's Building and Zoning Division first.

faqs.q: Do I have to complete the Ohio disclosure form for an inherited Grove City house?
faqs.a: Often no. Section 5302.30 exempts a transfer by a fiduciary administering an estate, and a seller who inherited the property and did not live in it during the prior year. Check the exemptions with an attorney or title agent before you skip it.

faqs.q: How much is the Franklin County conveyance fee on a Grove City sale?
faqs.a: It is $3 per $1,000 of the sale price, with a $0.50 transfer tax and a $3 minimum. The fee falls to $1 per $1,000 if the seller gets the homestead exemption at transfer. The Auditor's calculator shows the exact figure.

faqs.q: What does Grove City check on the outside of a home?
faqs.a: Inspectors look at property maintenance. Weeds must be under six inches, inoperable vehicles must be stored out of sight, and siding, roofs, gutters and downspouts should be in sound condition. Call 614-277-3075 with questions.

faqs.q: Which county office handles a Grove City deed?
faqs.a: The Franklin County Auditor's Transfer and Conveyance Department stamps the deed and collects the fees, and then the deed is recorded with the county. Your title company normally coordinates both steps at closing.
